modes.label: Windows running default
modes.note: Published default; effective authenticated rate card may override.

plans.name: API pay as you go
plans.note: Prepaid USD wallet; $.20 provisioning balance gate, not fee. First $5 advertised.

plans.name: Developer API
plans.note: $25 monthly API credits; same $.05 managed step; consumer credits are separate.

features.ip_note: Machines run on AWS/Daytona/Azure (datacenter egress); proxy {mode:'managed'} routes via Coasty's residential upstream, or bring your own http/https/socks5 proxy; no per-GB price published.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.

Public pricing headline says managed machines included, but detailed API docs and machine rate card explicitly charge runtime. Use detailed meter and flag conflict; do not assume step price includes rented VM hours.
GET /v 1/machines/pricing requires authentication (401 observed); published-default card is available anonymously at /api/pricing. No actual account-specific tariff was verified.
Stateful inference session is not a VM session and has no per-minute meter; managed machine and scheduled consumer execution are different objects.
Consumer subscription credits are quota units with variable dollar values, never the API wallet $.01 conversion. Parked-machine hourly charge cannot be encoded as per-GiB snapshot rate.
Marketing claims of benchmark superiority and comparison prices are not used as pricing evidence.

Machine size re-checked 2026-09-28: docs expose cpu_cores 1-16, memory_gb 1-64, storage_gb 8-500 ("auto" default, capped by tier) but no default size; public price feed (coasty.ai/api/pricing) lists a flat 5 credits/h Linux, 9 credits/h Windows ($0.01/credit), 1 credit/h stopped. Whether the rate varies with size is only in the authenticated /v1/machines/pricing feed, so sizes stay unpublished (vcpu/ram null).

fleet.verification: API-key signup advertises no card/no subscription; provisioning needs $0.20 API-wallet balance.
fleet.notes: Consumer plans include machines/swarm agents, but this card is the separately billed API. API wallet minimum $0.20 is a provisioning gate, not concurrency. BYOK still retains concurrency and persistent-machine safeguards whose numeric default was not found.
